walkthroughs.body_html: Industrialisation under Witte produced an urban working class and political parties: SDs (1898, split 1903), SRs (1901), Kadets (1905). The Russo-Japanese War (1904-05) and Bloody Sunday precipitated the 1905 Revolution. The October Manifesto and Fundamental Laws (April 1906) preserved autocratic prerogatives. Stolypin's agrarian reforms (1906-11) sought a 'wager on the strong'.

By 1917 Russian losses approached 1.7 million dead. Nicholas's assumption of command (September 1915) tied him to defeats. Rasputin's influence at court (until his murder, 30 December 1916) discredited the dynasty. Bread queues and the women's day strikes (8 March 1917) ignited the February Revolution; the Duma's Provisional Committee and the Petrograd Soviet emerged in tandem.

Lenin's April Theses rejected cooperation with the Provisional Government. The June Offensive failed; the July Days saw Lenin flee to Finland; the Kornilov Affair (August) discredited Kerensky. Bolshevik majorities in the Petrograd and Moscow Soviets enabled the October Revolution. The Second Congress of Soviets passed the Decrees on Peace and Land.

options: An elected Duma and civil liberties
Abolition of the monarchy
Withdrawal from WWI
Collectivisation of land

mcqs.q: Where was Lenin in exile during the July Days of 1917?
options: Finland
Switzerland
Siberia
Germany
It failed to overthrow the Tsar but forced the October Manifesto creating the Duma, exposing autocracy's weaknesses and rehearsing the structures of 1917.

mcqs.q: How did the Bolsheviks seize power in October 1917?
options: The October Revolution was a mass popular uprising that stormed the Winter Palace.
Trotsky's Military Revolutionary Committee coordinated a near-bloodless takeover of key buildings in Petrograd from a Provisional Government that had lost army and worker support.
The Provisional Government fell because the Tsar returned and reclaimed his throne.
The October Revolution overthrew the Tsar.

mcqs.q: Why did the Provisional Government fail in 1917?
options: It continued the unpopular war, did not redistribute land, shared 'dual power' with the Petrograd Soviet, and was discredited by the Kornilov affair before the Bolshevik takeover.
The Provisional Government fell because Lenin was personally more charismatic than Kerensky.
The Provisional Government fell because the Tsar returned and reclaimed his throne.
The 1905 Revolution was led by Lenin from the Winter Palace.
